utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Good morning, technical booth, interpreters, legal assistants, court reporters, Mr. Harmon, Mr. McCloskey, and Mr. Cayley, Mr. Petrusic, Mr. Visnjic, the expert witness. Good morning, General Krstic. And good morning to you too, Mr. Baraybar. I hope you've had a good rest. Have you? Yes, very well. Let me remind you that you are still on oath and you are going to be answering some more questions put to you by Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cayley, the floor is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, Mr. Petrusic, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Baraybar.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Just to remind you where we had left off yesterday, you had explained, in generic form by way of a model, how you come, as a forensic anthropologist, to calculate the minimum number of individuals, the MNI. Now I'd like to show you Exhibit 232, which is, in fact, the minimum number of individuals which you calculated from the anthropological examination from human remains which resulted from the Srebrenica investigation. The graves concerned are listed, and indeed in the footnotes of this document, you have given credit where you have obtained data from sources other than your own, such as Dr. Haglund, who testified yesterday. Mr. Baraybar, if you could move it down the screen towards the public gallery, the credits at the bottom. That's better. If you could explain this table to the Judges, please.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first thing I would like to say is that as it reads there, this is an addendum. There was a miscalculation in the original report submitted in 1999. The error -- with an arithmetic error in the calculation of the total MNI, and the variation was between 866 in the original report to 1.883. It's a miscalculation of .9 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, just to absolutely clarify that, you're talking about a simple addition problem within this table. The errors had nothing to do with the work you did in the field in the sense of counting bones.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. Right. I explained yesterday how we constructed the age intervals that we can see in this table. We have three age intervals, the 8 to 12 one, 13 to 24, and 25 plus. I also explained to you yesterday that it was necessary, in order to account for all individuals in primary and secondary sites, that it was to merge the minimal number of individuals between the primary sites and the linked secondary sites. This table shows all the calculations done for the whole season, meaning from 1996 to 1999. I have been using all the data available to create these calculations. Therefore, the sites of Branjevo Farm that were excavated in 1996 were linked to the sites of Cancari Road 12 that were excavated in 1998. There is a secondary site, and therefore a minimal number of individuals was calculated.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, if I could interrupt you, as you speak about each of these individual locations, could you use the pointer to indicate the particular primary grave that you're speaking of or the primary and secondary linked grave that you're speaking about?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure. The first site, the site of Kozluk, we have heard yesterday on Professor Wright's testimony, is a primary site. It happened to be linked to the secondary site of Cancari Road 3 that was excavated by Professor Wright in 1998. The total minimal number of individuals for the merged sites, for the primary and secondary sites, is 506 individuals. Again, I would say at least 506 individuals are represented between what was left in Kozluk and what was extracted from Kozluk and disposed of in CR-03. We proceed with the site of Glogova that I excavated last year. That is linked to the site of the [indiscernible] 5. That is a secondary site that was excavated by Professor Wright in 1998. Further clarification for the Glogova sites will be given when I present that information. However, the minimal number of individuals would be 187. Glogova 5, that is an undisturbed primary grave in the Glogova area. Again, I will discuss that further when I talk about my horology report. It has a minimal number of individuals of 90. And then the Nova Kasaba sites that were excavated in 1999, there are other ones obviously excavated in 1996. That is why we got Nova Kasaba 4. That is where we left it in 1996, three sites with a fourth site and so on. It had 19 individuals. Nova Kasaba 6, two; Nova Kasaba 7, one; Nova Kasaba 8, 33. All these sites were excavated by myself last year. From there we move to other primary graves. All these graves are primary. Konjevic Polje number 1, that was excavated by me last year with nine individuals; Konjevic Polje 2 with three. Hodzici road 5 that was excavated by Professor Wright in 1998 as a secondary site has 57 individuals. This specific site has not been linked to any primary site because the apparent source has not been excavated yet. We move then to Hodzici 3 and 4. That's two secondary sites that have been linked between each other based on soil evidence provided by Professor Brown, and it has 127. These two secondary sites, 3 and 4, again have not been linked to a primary site as yet because we do not have the evidence for that. The Pilica dam site, that is a primary site again, excavated by Professor Wright in 1998, and was linked to another secondary site dug the same year by Professor Wright that give us 219 individuals. We proceed to Branjevo Farm, excavated by Dr. Haglund in 1996. That is linked to Cancari Road 12, a secondary site dug in 1998 by Professor Wright, 283. The total of the Nova Kasaba sites dug in 1996 by Dr. Haglund give us 33 individuals. The Lazete site dug by Dr. Haglund in 1996 give us 164. Finally, the Cerska site dug by Dr. Haglund in 1996 give us 150. This basically means that the total minimal number of individuals recovered at the moment, between 1996 and 1999, adds up to 883 [sic]. Again, I would like to stress to the Court that this is only a very conservative estimate, meaning no less than 1.883 individuals are to be represented by all the bones, the thousands and thousands of bones we have recovered since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, you stated that Hadzici sites 3 and 4 have not been linked to a primary site, but am I right in saying that they are, in fact, linked to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The problem at the moment is that the soil analysis done by Professor Brown refers to a site in Orahovac that has not been excavated yet, that is, what we know as Lazete 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, there's a slight problem for the figure of minimum number of individuals is 883 and it is, in fact, 1.883.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Baraybar, of these individuals who -- this minimum number of individuals that you've identified, what proportion of them did you establish as male and what proportion as female?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will consult my report. I don't recall the numbers offhand. One thousand six hundred and fifty-six have been determined to be male; one has been determined to be a female, recovered from the site of Konjevic Polje 1; and 212 are of indeterminate sex.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What was the predominant age that you established from the mortal remains that you examined?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The majority of the remains in this case, 1.547 are individuals of 25 or more at death. I have created a breakdown of this 25-and-more category using some specific indicators like the pubic bone I mentioned yesterday. That information still tells us that most of the people are still clustered between the third, fourth and fifth decade, that the majority of the 24-and-more individuals cluster around those ages.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, when Mr. Manning put together his summary of all of the experts, he relied on your original report which had the arithmetical error in it, did he not?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And this Exhibit 232 replaces page 4 of your anthropological report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: One final point, Mr. President, for the benefit of the Court and indeed the public, this part of Mr. Baraybar's evidence has been agreed by the Defence. The reason that we have gone through it is to explain what within the report appears very complex to lay some foundation. So this is an abbreviated form of what his evidence might have been if the report had not been agreed to by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We can now move on to the part of your evidence which is not agreed by the Defence, which is the exhumations report which you completed in 1999, which is Exhibit 234. A matter that arose yesterday with another witness in terms of the composition of your team, from what areas of the world were your members of staff drawn?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Europe, North America, Central America, South America. That is, yes, pretty much it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: These were both anthropologists like yourself, scenes-of-crimes officers, anthropological assistants; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court which sites you examined between August and October of last year? It might be helpful if you place the map -- that map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We investigated a number of sites in the location of Nova Kasaba, very close to the area where Dr. Haglund conducted his exhumations in 1996 that I point to there. So it would be Nova Kasaba 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8. Not so far from there, up the road, close to the intersection that goes on the road that goes to Bratunac is the site of Konjevic Polje 1, also indicated there. Up the road going to Bratunac is the road -- the site of Konjevic Polje 2. And right past the village of Glogova that is not on this map, again on the road going to Bratunac, there's a number of sites known as Glogova 2, but they include many other graves I will discuss later.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So although that site is known as Glogova 2, it's actually a multiple, complex grave site; that is correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could move on to the first site, which is Nova Kasaba 4. When was that site exhumed by you and how did you come to know of its location?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nova Kasaba was exhumed between the 18th and the 21st of August last year. I was made aware by investigators of the existence of alleged graves in the area of Nova Kasaba after being shown an aerial photograph of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: How many bodies did you assess were present in that grave?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nineteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What was the sex of those individuals?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Males. All of them were males, if I'm not mistaken. Let me check my notes again. Yes, they were all males.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What was the age range of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all adults, again on the 25-plus range, but two of them were about 17 years of age.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the first photograph could be placed on the exhibit [sic], and in order to save exhibit numbers, we're going to use the report. It's on page 10 of your report, and I refer to the number in the bottom right-hand corner. Could you explain to the Judges what this represents and the significance of your findings in this part of grave?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most instructing feature in this grave was the presence of two litters or stretchers that we can see here. There is one here, and the other one goes here. Only one branch is depicted in the photograph. The other arm of the stretcher is under some of the bodies. These ones were made with tree branches and a blanket between the two, tied with rope, makeshift stretcher or litter. I'm leaving the term open, because I do not really know if it was a stretcher or litter. However, there are some other significant findings that may define this more clearly. Three individuals showed some kind of dressing, wound dressing, and one of them specifically had a splint on the lower -- on the lower leg. Therefore, the term "stretcher" in this -- at least one of the occasions would be most appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Did you find any items of clothing or luggage in this grave?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's quite a lot of it, as a matter of fact. Pretty much what you're seeing in this photograph, these items here are items of clothing. There was quite a lot of items of food, like humanitarian aid food, canned food of all sorts, tuna, canned tuna, and crackers, and all those kinds of things. A lot of the clothing was folded. I would not say pressed but it was folded as if it was part of somebody's luggage.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Did you find any items of identification on this grave site?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were nine, nine items of identification, various items of identification, all of them reported in the ICRC missing persons book.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So in essence, you linked the pieces of identification with individuals who had been reported as missing --

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: -- by the International Committee for the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you can place the photograph that is on page 9, so it's one page back, which is of a skeletonised body lying in a grave, and if you could explain to the Judges the significance of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows an individual lying on his back with both feet close to each other and the arms hyperextended over his head. That's one, and another one there. However, it's important to notice that the wrists -- both wrists are almost converging close to each other, so to speak. They're forming almost like a circle. These individuals, together with some others that are not shown in this photograph, made us think that some of them at least could have been balanced manually in the grave by holding the feet and holding the arms and just throwing them to the grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Did you find any military paraphernalia in this grave?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not find any items that made us think of any -- of anybody dressed -- dressed in terms of clothing with military uniforms like camouflage fatigues or anything of the kind. However, we did find an individual that may have been carrying, it was close to him, a 54 live round of 7.62 millimetre ammunition. That is the Kalashnikov family ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Lastly, on this particular grave, if you could show the photograph on page 11. You mentioned earlier you found an individual within the grave who had a makeshift split attached to his leg. This is a photograph, is it not, that was taken shortly after the body was removed from the grave?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. In order to preserve anything that could be lost due to transport when the body is transported to the mortuary, we took a picture after lifting the body from the grave. Just for orientation purposes, this is the foot here and this is the lower leg. This is a tree branch. This is another tree branch, and there is some kind of bandage joining this or keeping these tree branches together. Subsequent examination at the mortuary shows that it is a fracture in this area. So this is basically a splint to stabilise the fracture.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could quickly move on to Nova Kasaba 6. Do you have it in front of you, Mr. Baraybar?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: How did you become aware of this site?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, this alleged grave was indicated to me by investigators based on an aerial photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: When did you exhume it and how long did it take to exhume?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was exhumed only one day, on the 25th of August, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What type of grave was this and how many individuals did it contain?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very different grave than the one previously shown. This grave was dug by hand, most likely by shovels or spades, and contained the remains of two people.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What was the sex of these two individuals, if that could be ascertained?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Male.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And were you able to assess their ages?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them was young, was between, I would say, 14 to 24 years of age, and the second one was again 25 plus, between, let's say, 22 and 50 years of age.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could show the diagram on page 14, which I think is produced from the survey that Professor Wright demonstrated to the Court was taking place on every grave. Can you explain to the Judges how this image is produced and the significance of it?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as Professor Wright has shown before, we take a lot of care in recording the position of every artefact and body found in the grave by means of electronic survey. That data from this machine can then be downloaded into a computer in order to produce a map or a sketch. That is what you see at the moment and is basically a schematic representation of the two bodies, the position in which they were lying, and a number of artefacts that were recovered in association with these bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you explain the particularly significant points in this diagram?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Individual number 2 -- or under, rather, individual number 2, a number of bullets were recovered, and by "bullets" I mean fired rounds, slugs. A total of basically five were recovered from under this individual. This one here labelled "9A" and this one here labelled "4A" were not in direct association with the body, and 8A as well as. They were very close to the body. However, number 7 and number 5 were literally under the body. In all these cases, the bullets were embedded in the soil. They were not lying on the surface. They were at least an inch or less between -- let's say half an inch and an inch embedded in the soil. An interpretation we draw from this is that this individual was most likely shot while lying in the grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Just for the purpose of the record, the witness has been referring to figure 3 on page 14 of Exhibit 234.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, if you can now move on to Nova Kasaba 7, and I'll give you a moment to find the relevant page in your report. How was this grave notified to you?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, this is one of the graves that was shown to me as to be present in an aerial photograph. The important feature regarding this site was that in the photograph shown to me that is dated 27th of July, 1995, the site of Nova Kasaba 7 looks to be an open or, rather -- "open" would be the right word, trench, an unfilled trench, simply an open trench.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: When did you exhume this site?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was exhumed on the 22nd of August, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And how many people did you find in this grave?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And what was the sex of that individual?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a male between 31 and 65 years of age.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Did you find anything of significance, apart from the body, within that grave?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We recovered two 30-millimetre cartridges, spent cartridges. That is, there seemed to be some part of cartridges of a large weapon, most likely anti-aircraft or something of that kind, that were at the bottom of this trench. In order to clarify what I mean by "trench", this was basically a trench excavated by a front loader, so it was a trench with a ramp. So on the ramp at the bottom, there were two large shell casings. One of them was smashed, as a matter of fact, by something very heavy that ran over it. We also recovered a number of shell casings of smaller weapons, as well as bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: How are you able to conclude that this grave had been dug by a front loader?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: A feature of front loaders when digging basically any trench, whether the trench is to be used as a grave or not, is to create a ramp. Otherwise, they could not dig in.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And this feature is apparent when you exhume the grave?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. We also -- sorry to interrupt you. We also recovered parts of tracks of the machine, wheels of the machine, so it was quite apparent.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could now move on to Nova Kasaba 8. How were you made aware of this site?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, this site, the alleged grave at the time was shown to me in this aerial photograph I already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And when was this site exhumed?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the 27th of August and the 6th of September, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And how many individuals did you recover from this grave?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirty-three.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Were you able to establish the sex of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirty-two of them were male, and one remains indeterminate.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, I think in this grave there were a number of clusters of individuals, and if you turn to page 20 of your report, there's a photograph which represents this very clearly. Can you explain this to the Judges, please?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We recovered in this grave three clusters of bodies. The clusters were labelled in the same order they were placed into the grave. Cluster 1 was the first at the bottom of the grave. As a matter of fact, you actually see that the grave again is one of these trenches dug by some kind of front loader with a ramp. You see the ramp here and the tooth marks of the machine, of the blade of the machine. The cluster 1 is this one [indicates]. Cluster 2 is the one in the middle. You see that between cluster 1 and 2 there is spoil, so we have excavated this as a cake, so to speak, to show you the way in -- the position of each of the clusters in relation to each other. So if this [indicates] was not excavated, the dirt that we see between the two clusters was covering the whole of cluster 1, so it's basically literally a layered grave. And cluster number 3, that is the last to be deposited into the grave, that is basically there [indicates]. You see in each instance there is an amount of spoil placed between each of the clusters.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What is the significance of the turf or spoil between the clusters?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It indicates pretty much two things. The first is that there is a time difference between the disposal of the clusters of bodies. By "time", I'm not referring here to absolute time, because I cannot actually time the time elapsed between each disposal. I cannot say whether it happened in a matter of hours or days. I can't really say. And the second element is that for the length of the grave and the amount of sediment between each of the clusters, that could have not been placed there by hand, but rather, again, through mechanical means. It also implies that the bodies themselves could have been lifted mechanically from another location and transported to this place, and they came with a lot of dirt, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And, lastly, did you find anything else of significance in this grave which I think will become relevant later on in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. The first important thing is that in cluster 1, meaning here, these bodies had a number of branches and leaves from a willow tree. The branches were between two and four millimetres of thickness. They were quite thick branches. They were completely entangled -- commingled with the bodies. We also discovered that in cluster 1, meaning the ones I just showed you, at least again some people could have been shot while in the grave. Again we recover bullets embedded in the soil under them. And in the last cluster to be placed there, number 3, we also recovered bullets under some of the bodies embedded in the sediment. I will discuss the issue of the willow leaves when I discuss Nova Kasaba 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And I think the clusters are, in fact, clearly numbered by marks that have been placed in the graves. If you could just point those out for the reference when people come back to look at this.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 [indicates], number 2 [indicates], and number 3 [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Baraybar. If we could now move on to Nova Kasaba 5, and again I'll give you a moment to find your place.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could be provided with Exhibit 14/10, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What, if anything, did you find in Nova Kasaba 5? And please remember that it's not actually marked on this photograph, so if you could actually identify the location of Nova Kasaba 5 on this particular photograph.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Nova Kasaba 5, this area here. That is an area of lighter soil, an elongated area of lighter soil, some narrow lanes parallel to each other -- two, as a matter of fact, here -- and then a small area of lighter soil again. In this area, literally immediately adjacent to this small area of lighter soil, is a willow tree that cannot actually be seen in this copy, but there is a tree, as a matter of fact. It is visible in the original photograph, I think, if I see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could you use a marker and mark Nova Kasaba 5? Otherwise, I think we're going to lose this. And we'll provide a new exhibit to the Court and we'll re-mark this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And if you could mark that as "NK-5".

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Baraybar.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: So all the other Nova Kasaba graves we have discussed a moment ago already marked in this photograph. The only one that was not marked was NK-05. Then as these areas here of soil disturbance were interpreted to be graves and, as a matter of fact, proven to be graves later on, we assumed that this area here was also a grave. We conducted a series of trenches across this area of lighter soil [indicates]. However, the place did not show any features of a grave. There was no grave whatsoever. So this basically was interpreted as to be only a scrape of the soil exposing lighter soil. So from the air, it would look as an elongated area of lighter soil. That is what we see at the moment. However, a significant feature is that from this scrape, that is quite regular in terms of width and length, emerged two areas of, again, lighter soil, thin lanes parallel to each other such as tracks, and you can see them here. One is here and the other one is here. Both of them are leading to this small mound of, again, freshly-scraped soil most likely from here, in here at the foot of the willow tree. So once we discovered this was not a grave and we assumed, therefore, it was a scrape, we remembered the willow leaves we found in NK-08. And then we got to formulate the following hypothesis: If people were shot in this area close to the road and then were removed mechanically from there, and if these bodies were, by whatever reason, in contact with this willow tree that, as a matter of fact, is the only willow tree to be found in this area, in that area, and in all this area here the only willow trees that exist are actually interspersed along the stream we can see here, some 20 metres away from NK-08, it would be impossible that branches and leaves from the tree, once it has been shaken, would fall on the bodies and then would end up in NK-08. So we did two things in order to try to ascertain this. It's still a hypothesis. We then tried to validate our hypothesis. The first thing is that if people were shot in this area of lighter soil, we would need to find shell casings of some sort. However, we assume again that the scrape was caused by bodies being removed from there. Therefore, the shell casings should not be there, but at least some shell casings should be in the small mound at the foot of the willow tree. So we excavated the small mound, and indeed we found five shell casings from 7.62-millimetre ammunition. Then we compared the leaves and branches from NK-08, from cluster 1, in order to ascertain whether they were indeed willow, and they were. Therefore, we also reproduced the same movement with our own small backhoe, and after shaking the tree we obtained some thick branches and leaves. This basically means that the probabilities of branches and leaves flying around this area and arriving in an area of over 200 metres from the tree close to the road to the grave are highly unlikely. Therefore, NK-05 has been preliminarily interpreted as a possible excavation site maybe linked to NK-08, at least to the first cluster of individuals buried there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could now move on to KP-1, Konjevic Polje site 1. Do you have your report in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: When was this site notified to you?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This site was notified to me at the same time that the Nova Kasaba sites were shown to me in this photograph. Actually, it's through another photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And when you speak of photographs, you're speaking of aerial --

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: How long did it take to exhume this site?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We exhumed it between the 7th and the 9th of September of 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And if Exhibit 15/2, Mr. Usher, could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And so as not to waste any time, I'll continue asking you questions. How many bodies were exhumed in this site?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Were you able to establish the sex of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were eight males and one female.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What were the age ranges of the males?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven of them between 25 and 65 years of age, and one between 16 and 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Were you able to establish the age range of the female?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Between 16 and 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, this exhibit in front of the Judges at the moment, this is, in fact, the site of KP-1. Can you explain to the Judges the layout of this particular grave?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This grave, again, was -- contained two clusters of people. Eight individuals in the first cluster and only one in the last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What items of significance did you find within this grave?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We recovered, again, one bag with quite a lot of items of clothing. Inside the bag was somebody's luggage, pretty much. And we also recovered a Seiko automatic watch that was marking the date as Saturday, the 15th at 12.35.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Did you consult an expert on that watch?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And what conclusions did he come to?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the expert report of Mr. Mills, a horologist, it seems that that combination of date and time lead us to a time between 32 and 36 hours before. That would be the 13th. And if I may correct, I said Saturday, but it was actually Friday the 15th at 12.35.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now what you're saying is the expert concluded that the watch had stopped 32 to 36 hours before?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The oscillation of the wrist stopped 32 to 36 hours before.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you can place photograph 11, which is on page 28, on the ELMO. Is this exactly as you found the watch?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. This is a picture taken. The watch is there. The person is lying face down. That is the picture we took before cleaning any further or altering the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Were you able to conclude how the bodies were brought to this grave site?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the individuals placed in the first cluster, meaning the first eight individuals, may have been brought by mechanical means, pretty much by a front -- a front loader. There was some turf, some grass under the bodies pretty much as it was being scraped or taken off the topsoil. We also found some white powder. I was actually forgetting that. Some white powder such as lime on top of some of the bodies and a stretcher. There was a stretcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Why would lime be placed on the bodies?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In other -- it's my experience, at least in other settings, that there is an association between quenching the smell of rotting bodies and placing lime on top of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: In essence, to conceal their presence in the grave.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could now move to the last site? Konjevic Polje, which is Konjevic Polje 2. That is on page 29 of your report. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Was this site identified to you through aerial imagery?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: When was it exhumed?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 10th of September, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: How many bodies did you find in this grave?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three in two graves. One grave with one and another one with two.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What was the sex of these individuals, if you were able to determine that?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Male.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And what were their ages?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In grave 1 was a male between 31 and 71 years of age. In grave 2, two young males between 15 and 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Were you able to establish whether or not they'd been placed by a mechanical digger into the grave?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In grave 1, the body most likely was placed, again, through mechanical means. There was a pedestal of branches; turf, meaning grass; flowers, literally scooped with the topsoil where he was lying. And in grave 2, at least one of the two may have been again pushed in by scraping quite a lot of topsoil and vegetation into the shallow grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Do you have any other comments on that particular site?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In grave 2, at least one of the two individuals may have been shot while in the grave. He sustained a number of shots and a number of bullets, again, when recovered from under the body. I think the pathologist will -- Dr. Clark will clarify this issue even further.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, the last site, which, I think, is the most complex site, that at Glogova. Was this site notified to you through aerial imagery?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown 161/1, Prosecutor's Exhibit. You may have it there. It's the aerial imagery of Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, which site did you supervise the exhumation over?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area marked as GL-2.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, has it been -- has the site GL-1 been tested for the presence of human remains?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it has.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And what did that test reveal?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: A positive. There are human remains in the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, how long did GL-2 take to exhume?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We started on the 11th of September, and we finished on the 15th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So it was a very large site.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, if the witness could be shown 161/5, and that is the large crater.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You might wish to put these two photographs on the ELMO at the same time, Mr. Baraybar, to demonstrate the point that you're making, if that's possible. Perhaps the lower exhibit could be moved up and tucked under the upper exhibit. Yes. That's fine. Mr. Baraybar, if you could explain to the Judges the significance of the differences between these two photographs.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this photograph labelled as 27th of July, 1995, we see a large area of disturbance on either side of the road. In this second photograph of the 30th of October, 1995, we see a large crater in the area marked as GL-2. We do not see anything similar, at least in GL-1, but it is quite clear there is a large hole in the area of GL-2. Also, it is indicated in the photograph the shape, according to the photograph, of a front loader, but what is really clear to my eyes is that there is a large hole in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So let the record show that on 161/5, the witness has indicated that a large crater is present at the site marked GL-2, which is not present on the same site represented in Exhibit 161/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, how many graves were there at site GL-2?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We estimate that at the moment we may have between six and seven. There's still a section of that area to be excavated this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, the simplest way to represent this to the Judges, I think, is to do a sketch of the various grave sites, and I've put some paper and a pencil in front of you. I think that a sketch is actually clearer than the diagram in your report. So if you're able to do that on the ELMO, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I will draw here is the position -- the relative position of the grave we found before the crater that we have seen in this other photograph was made, and I will explain all the details regarding the crater later. The first -- and the other thing I want to say is that the order in which I will draw these graves is not necessarily the order in which the graves were originally dug, because I cannot demonstrate when each one of them was dug, in which order, which one came first and so forth. So GL-03 is a trench, again, dug with a front loader. It's one of these graves with a ramp. Then we have the remains of a grave. We don't really know how this grave was because the grave may have been something like this, that is, GL-06 -- I'm going to mark it here -- and this GL-03. Then we have another grave that was a trench that was opened in this case with a backhoe, a large excavator with -- a backhoe with teeth. We found, as a matter of fact, the teeth marks on it. It was roughly like this. This is what we call GL-02 grave. Also we found, isolated from this, a series of two graves that happened to be expanded. So this one was expanded like this. That is what we call GL-05. This is section "A" and "B." Basically this was a grave at some point, and then they expanded it and created a big one. So the two graves coalesced. So for the sake of clarity, I'll refer to GL-05 all the time. Right. In the picture of the 27th of July that we just have seen, we see an area of disturbance marked as GL-1 on one side and GL-2 on the other side. In the second photograph of 30th of October we see a crater. I will explain what I found. What we found, basically, was indeed a large crater that crossed in this fashion. The grave of GL-03 was sectioned pretty much by its middle part. However, an area of it, meaning this one here, was left untouched, and in this untouched area, we recovered a number of 11 bodies. The bottom of this area I'm calling GL-02 grave, and again was left untouched, and we found seven bodies. In this area of GL-06, we did not find anything in its original position. Everything was mixed up. In this large crater, we found the remains of some 32 individuals. Making a minimum number of 50 found in the whole area. So this area of the crater, we're going to call it GL-02 crater. A number of items of clothing, again of canned food, stretchers, and things of the like were found in this large crater. In the area of GL-05, we detected an undisturbed primary grave. We recovered from there 90 individuals. This again would be a minimal number, estimate number of 90 individuals. And between GL-05 and all this large crater, we have seen an area that has not been excavated yet that we're going to term GL-07, that is pending to be finished this year. And area here again may have been robbed, but I cannot really give any assurance of that at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If that exhibit could be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Were you able to establish the sex of the individuals who you've identified were exhumed from this grave?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will give you the data in a minute. I have to check in my notes. From -- yes. Some 20 found in this area of the crater were determined to be male.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And the other 12?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm almost sure they were also male. I do not have the specific data in front of me. No. As a matter of fact, yes. Seven of these ones were male. So seven of GL-03 were male. And from these other ones, 20 were male as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And that's from the GL-02 crater?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And in GL-05?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In GL-05, 82 of the 90 were male.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Were any of these individuals established to be females?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So the remaining numbers are of indeterminate sex?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could place page 39 of your report --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Cayley. His drawing will be 161/2/A.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could briefly explain this photograph to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is GL-03. We are observing the ramp in the first plain here. So we are basically standing at the entrance, so to speak, of the grave. This is the ramp. You can see on this area here the tyre marks of the excavator. This area here clearly shows that the grave was robbed, was sectioned pretty much into two parts. The crater I just drew is here, and this is a section that was left untouched and the bodies are still in situ there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, by inference, it is obvious from what you're saying about the crater is that there was this major disturbance. What conclusions did you reach about this crater? What had happened to this grave?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, although we cannot say what is the order in which the graves, with the exception of GL-05, were excavated, we can say for sure that all the graves that were excavated, meaning GL-03, 6, and 2, were robbed simultaneously, because the crater is basically the linking factor between all those graves. And we have to say as well that we do not sort of discard the possibility that in the middle part of the crater there was still another grave because it's simply a crater. The crater went beyond the existence of any grave, up to the sterile soil. It was a big, deep hole. So we don't really know whether there was something else in there. We cannot prove it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could turn to the photograph on page 36 of your report, which is GL-02, and I'd like you to comment upon the tooth marks that you've identified on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I drew a moment ago, the GL-02 grave is a trench primarily, so the boundaries of it would be from here to here coming down. You see the dark soil. That shows the outline of it, and continues like here and goes there. In this area here, obviously the photograph doesn't show much, the tooth marks in the wall of the grave from the machine who actually originally excavated the grave. So this is nothing to do with robbing in this case. These are the marks of the machine who opened the grave in the first place, who dug the hole. So basically the trench opened by a backhoe type or class of excavator.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Were there any particular items of interest that you found in this grave, such as ID cards?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were. An important thing, since we are discussing the GL-02 grave, is that all over this area here again we found a tremendous amount -- I would say close to half a cubic metre that is quite a lot of lime or a lime-like substance. We also recovered, in addition to that, a watch -- an automatic watch in the crater, in the GL-02 crater, in the robbing area, marking again Friday the 15th at 8.15. And we recovered a second watch on the ramp of GL-03 that I just showed you a moment ago marking "Saturday, 15", but no times, just "Saturday, 15".

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Were these watches examined by an expert?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. We -- Mr. Mills -- based on Mr. Mills' report, we conclude again that the time we're referring to is 32 to 36 hours prior to this date, around the 13th again.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, as a final matter on these graves, there was a sediment in GL-03 and GL-05, and if you could place your drawing that you did back on the ELMO and explain this to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Professor Brown again took some soil samples to make some comparisons between these sites and some other sites, so some samples were taken from here from under the bodies in GL-03. Some other samples were taken from GL-05 in different locations of the grave. Then the conclusions of this soil analysis, including pollen and mineralogical analysis, is that the sediment of GL-03 and GL-05 are identical and the sediment is foreign to this area and should come from a meadow type of environment that was cultivated in the past for cereal, including maize. He also found that those sediments were identical to those recovered in GL-05.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Are you aware as to whether or not the Sandici area had been cultivated for maize production?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Finally, if the witness could be shown this, rather than getting him to search for it, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Baraybar, the sites that are shaded in green are exhumed sites?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And the unshaded sites are sites which have been identified but not yet exhumed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And do all of those sites, based on the preliminary examination, contain human remains?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And based on your experience, would you expect to find at least a number of bodies in all of those graves?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So the figure that you have given as the mean number of individuals which, as you acknowledge, is very conservative, is going to significantly increase as these graves are exhumed?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions for the witness, so I can offer him for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this is a good time for a break before we continue with the cross-examination, so let us have a 20-minute recess now, after which we will resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could -- excuse me, Mr. Visnjic. It's just housekeeping. The last exhibit that Mr. Baraybar was referring to was Prosecutor's Exhibit 140, which was not placed on the record. And earlier the court deputy informed me that when I was referring to Exhibits 161/1 and 161/5, it should have been 161/1 and 161/2. I put it in the record now so that in future months, when people come to read it, they are aware of what I was referring to, indeed what the witness was referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very well, Mr. Cayley. Mr. Baraybar, you're now going to answer questions put to you by Mr. Visnjic. Mr. Visnjic, your turn.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, good morning. Mr. Baraybar, the first group of questions we have for you has to do with the Nova Kasaba 04 grave site. In this grave, according to your report, 19 bodies were found. However, you isolated two bodies of males, and you determined that on average they were 17 years old. Is there any particular reason for this?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I have written in the report is that we have 19 adult males. Two of them, however, were or had mean ages of 17 years of age, not that all the 19 have mean ages of 17 years. Only two.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: There may be an error in the translation. My question was: Was there any particular reason why you separated out those two males from the rest?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If -- I do not know if I understand the question correctly. Two individuals have been classed as to have a mean age of 17 years of age, meaning they fall in the range 13 to 24 because of specific features, pretty much -- I presume -- I don't have the specific anthropology report in front of me regarding those two, but my assumption would be that a number of traits in those individuals, basically in their bones, would show that they were still in the process of growth. Therefore, they have been ascribed to that age range.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, the growth phase that you have mentioned now continues until what age?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most individuals stop -- I would not say "growing", because that gives the impression that people grow like plants forever and ever, in a way. Most processes regarding the fusion of some parts of the bone to another part of the bone end on average at age 21, on average. That's just a very generic explanation. We could go and refer to specific bones. But the average, let's say it stops about 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In your previous report, when describing several age groups, you said that you combined the age groups of 13 to 17 and the next group of 15 to 24, that you combined these two groups. Could you explain to us the reasons for doing this?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason is simply a mathematical reason. In my archaeology report, I am dealing with a level of detail I am not dealing with in the anthropology report. The anthropology report refers to the whole set of numbers that have been collected over all these years. Therefore, in order to depict the distribution of age of hundreds of individuals, I have to be able to include or to fit individual ages into wider ranges. That is why if I am referring only to 19 individuals, it makes much more sense, in my opinion, when reading the report of 19 individuals, to specify or to be more specific regarding the ages defined for each of these individuals. If I see these 19 bodies in the -- as part of the whole of the 1.800 bodies, of course I cannot be as detailed with that and I need to just merge them. That is why.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: When you were working on this global estimation, in a part of your report you stated that the method used to determine the age was modified by certain standards for the Bosnian population.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is partly correct. The standard has not been modified. In other words, the standard remains the same. What has been modified are the age ranges associated to the standard. So for example -- just for the sake of clarity, I will expand on this, if I may. If, for example -- let's assume that technique "A" is composed by the observation of four different features of the pubic bone or the hip bone. The characteristics that define each phase, meaning what I'm observing, remain the same. What changes, however, is the number of individuals that share that characteristic. So if the original sample used to develop that technique was, for example, a North America population, I might expect the North Americans of age, let's say, 20 to 30 to show characteristic "A." However, if I now turn to a Bosnian population or a Balkan population, an European population, maybe the same characteristics of phase "A" will be shared by people between 30 and 40. So I am observing still the same things; however, the age ranges associated to those things have changed. So the standards have not changed, just the number of individuals who share those features have changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: The standard you used for the Bosnian population was established in 1999. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The results of the study have been published or presented, rather, in an international meeting in 1999. I presume that this investigation was done through 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind large population migrations in Bosnia until that time, are you aware that there was a certain standard for the Yugoslav population or for the population of Bosnia prior to the outbreak of the war?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of any Yugoslav standards referring to this specific technique, meaning the techniques, rather, we have used in this study.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, bearing in mind the standard established by this investigation in 1999 and the standards that you refer to in your studies -- I'm not quite sure whether they are American standards -- anthropologically speaking, can it be said of the Bosnian population that they develop earlier or quicker. Or let me put it this way: What is the difference between the two standards? Is it of substantive significance?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will explain to you directly -- I will read to you the differences. We are dealing, in these questions, only with the standards for adults, and we are, just for the sake of clarity, referring to two techniques that are the techniques we have used for aging adults, that is, the so-called Suchey-Brooks pubic symphysis age estimation system, and the Iscan-Loth sternal rib age estimation system. The two techniques were developed indeed in multi-ethnic North American population. The pubic symphysis one was developed, as a matter of fact, in Los Angeles at the office of the chief medical examiner, and the rib technique was developed in Florida. I would like to read to you some examples of the point I'm trying to make. For example, in American or North American males, phase one of Suchey-Brooks, or the technique regarding the hip bone, has a range, meaning the people that share the characteristics of that phase, that spans between 15 until 23 years of age. In Bosnian males, based on this study I'm referring to, there is a study by Simmons and Associates from 1999, the same range spans between 13 and 25. If we go to other phases that speak -- for example, phase number 4, the range for the North Americans would be between 23 and 57, and in Bosnians, between 15 and 71. So in both cases, there are certain differences in the ranges, but what will change, as a matter of fact, in each case, will be the mean of each of the phases. But we are really not dealing with means but with ranges. It is quite difficult to say whether Bosnians or anybody from the Balkans ages quicker or evolves quicker or slower, because these techniques relate to changes in shape, integrity -- shape and integrity mainly or some aspects in bones. These techniques are not linked to anything such as growth of children, for example. This is only for individuals past a certain age, for fully developed individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me the standard that you have adopted, and which is based on Simmons and Associates investigation, how large was the sample used and how many cases do you need to establish such a standard?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two criteria are important in order to establish a standard. Firstly, a sample size, of course. But besides a sample size is the number of individuals represented in each age range. I may have 1.000 individuals between 20 and 30. I will not be able to predict anything about individuals between 30 and more; obviously not. I would need to have them -- let's say 100 individuals with ten people in each ten-year range category, ten in 20 to 30, ten in 30 to 40 and so on, would be much easier. So this collection that seems an associate assembled is substantially and statistically large enough for that and fills the criteria of a distribution within the sample of ages. So this male sample is 242 individuals. All these individuals were recovered at autopsy room conditions, so these are not war casualties nor anything of the kind. They are people that went into the medical examiner's office for a medical autopsy. The sample for the females is much, much smaller. It's only 52 individuals. That is for the pubes. Now, for the ribs we have 233 males and we have 52 females, again a small sample. But if I may call your attention on a very important factor. In the case of the pubes of the hip bone, the original sample collected in Los Angeles was 739 individuals, and the Bosnian one is literally a third of it, 242. However, in the rib technique, the American sample is 118, while the Bosnian one is twice as large; 233. From a scientific point of view, I think that it is quite sound evidence that this technique is reliable, the sample taken is quite, quite reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: According to your report, in which you provided in groups the ages for all graves, in this particular grave site, Nova Kasaba 04, it is stated that five persons were in the age group between 13 and 24 and 14 in the group over 25 years of age. That is page 9 of your report. My question is: Does that mean that your report on exhumations is far more precise regarding certain graves as compared to the report on the investigation of human remains?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe the term is not "precision", but I would call it "emphasis". It is certain that more details regarding individual graves and, therefore, individuals recovered in those graves will have much more emphasis in the archaeology report than in the anthropology report. If I were to use the same emphasis in the anthropology report, my report will be hundreds and hundreds of pages long in the case of the anthropology report. That is one factor. The second factor, I think, is that the emphasis of the anthropology report is not to detail or to discuss individual cases but rather to discuss it globally. It's a global presentation of how many people have been examined over these last years.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, does that mean that in the Nova Kasaba 4 grave site, there were no persons who were younger than 17?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were individuals, let's say using now the anthropological term, no younger than 13. Those people would be classed in the 13 to 24 age range. So it would be correct to say there were no younger than 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: How many individuals were there in the group between 17 and 25?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what grave?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In Nova Kasaba 4.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can actually pick up the specific data, if you give me just one moment. I see what you're getting at. When we assembled the age ranges, the age ranges of 13 to 24 and 25 plus, and I said that earlier, we were combining a number of data that was coming from different sources, the 1996 report and all the other reports done before. As you rightly said, in 1998, for example, the 13-to-24-year interval was divided into two, into two parts, one between 13 and 17, 18 to 24, and so forth. In order to be more inclusive, we have merged them in the range 13 to 24 to be just simply more inclusive. So according to this, in Nova Kasaba 4, the range 13 to 24 has or contains five individuals out of the 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that this group cannot be determined more closely as being a group ranging between 17 to 24 years?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In your report relating to the Nova Kasaba 04 grave site, you state that traces were found of bullets?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In number 4 -- could you tell me what page, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: On page 7, paragraph 2, last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I'm saying here is that in a few cases the presence of shotgun pellets was recorded in addition to other gunshot injuries. That refers to injuries and has been extracted, as indicated previously, from the pathologist's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand. So did you find shotgun pellets or traces of them? Did you actually find the shotgun pellets themselves, the buckshot, or traces of them?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the pathologist's report, as I raise in my report here, 11 individuals died of gunshot wounds, while the cause of death of the eight others was unascertained. In a few cases, the presence of shotgun pellets, and that links to the bodies not in the sediment or anywhere else, was recorded in addition to other gunshot injuries. I would refer this information to the chief pathologist.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Do you have an explanation for these traces of shotgun pellets?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In this grave site, you also came across an individual who had 54 bullets of a calibre of 7.62. Did this individual, if you can tell us that at all -- that is to say, was that person wearing civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that information. Give me a moment. This information is extracted again from the pathologist's report. The individual was dressed in blue jeans, and let's say blue denim trousers -- that would be the appropriate way to put it -- and a blue jacket, so jean-type jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In the Kasaba 04, you also found some personal documents scattered around. Does that mean that the bodies were searched or is there some other explanation?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any explanation. I can just tell you that documents were found in the grave fill, in most of the cases, as well as many other items of clothing and artefacts. There were quite a lot of artefacts found. I stated in my report, regarding the artefacts found loose in the grave, that the two stretchers that we found were covering some of the bodies, and the stretchers were -- for the shape in which they were found, were basically found turned inside out, so as if they had been stuffed with things and then just simply emptied in the grave. That is to be found in paragraph 1 on page number 10 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, do you perhaps have information on the following, although I don't think that was part of your job: The identification of individuals from that grave site? Were most of them identified, do you happen to know?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In keeping with everything that you found in the grave site, do you exclude the possibility that the bodies in this grave site, in this grave, had been casualties during combat activities in an attempt to cross the asphalt road and that they were buried in this grave later on, subsequently?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot exclude the possibility. In my opinion, however, if I may add, there's two things important to remember. The first one is that the documents found either on bodies or lose in the grave fill are of people reported missing by the ICRC, the International Committee for the Red Cross, and appear in the book of the missing of the ICRC. The date of -- in which these people were reported as missing spans roughly, according to those documents, between the 11th and the 18th of July, 1995. That's, again, point number one. Second, in my opinion, it is quite difficult -- it would be very difficult for me to imagine that people carrying stretchers or litters, for that matter, could be engaged in some kind of confrontation. The third point, in my opinion, again, it would be -- that would be even more difficult considering one of them had a fracture caused, according to the pathology report, by gunshot to the leg and has a splint and dressing. Those basically would be the three points which, in my opinion, would sort of preclude that explanation. However, the answer to your question originally would be no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, the stretchers -- we're talking about a grave with nine individuals and only two stretchers were found; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nineteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Yes, nineteen.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, yes, that's correct, two stretchers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And also found were three -- a maximum of three individuals who had had previous wounds or injuries.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did any one of the individuals -- that is to say, on how many individuals did you find traces of shotgun pellets?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know. You would need to refer to the pathology report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In keeping with your conclusion that at least 19 persons, 19 persons and at least 4 were carried -- were carrying the stretcher and that 3 were injured, 12 people were, nonetheless, capable of engaging in combat operations. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The answer is yes. However, I cannot -- I have no evidence whatsoever to make such a conclusion, but presented in that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, I'd like to talk about the next grave site, Nova Kasaba 06, now, please. In this grave, a male individual was found, ages ranging between 14 and 24.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind your previous testimony where the standard was 13 to 24, can you explain the difference in this concrete case?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is no difference, as a matter of fact. In my previous testimony, what I have stated is that the range we are using for calculations of the overall number of cases goes between 13 and 24. In this specific individual, the emphasis, again, in the archaeology report is much more in the description of individual cases. And according to the standards we've been using and the evidence we've been finding in this case, this individual happened to be between 14 and 24. For calculation proposals, this individual will adapt to the 13 to 24 category.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: You also state that four bullets were found below the body of an individual, which lead to the conclusion and confirmation, according to you, that he was shot in the grave itself. My question is the following: At what depth did you find these projectiles?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general -- in general, as I said earlier, the projectiles were found in various depths in the sediment and under the body, which could range between half an inch and an inch. In this specific -- in this specific case -- I am looking through the report to see if I have stated that. Maybe I have not stated how many millimetres under the body the projectiles were recovered, and I don't think I have. As a matter of fact, no. They were simply in the sediment under the body, but the norm has been pretty much between half an inch and an inch. Sometimes less, sometimes more than that. Doesn't mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, how far would a 7.62-calibre metre lodge -- be lodged in the earth, having passed through a body? Have you got an orientation as to that?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a precise orientation because, in my knowledge, the factors influencing this would be the compaction of the soil. Obviously, it would be very different if somebody shot through a concrete floor than if he shot through mud or if he shot through some kind of clay soil that is very compacted. The only evidence I have is based on our findings in recovering a slug of a projectile embedded in the soil.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: You also find 14 casings, 14 shell casings. Do you know whether these casings were identified, as well as the projectiles in this concrete case, although I know that that was not your job?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, according to your overall impressions for the Nova Kasaba 06 grave site, do you exclude the possibility that on a dead body lying in the grave, a burst of gunfire was fired?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I definitely cannot explain nor draw such a conclusion. I have only bones. I don't think that anybody could really determine whether the person was dead or alive while being shot in the grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: As an anthropologist, did you take part in determining the character of the injuries that were inflicted, whether they were ante-mortem or post-mortem?

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As anthropologists, we do assist the pathologist in the reconstruction and assessment of injuries. However, it is the pathologist's responsibility and prerogative to give an opinion about the nature of those injuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My next group of questions relates to the Nova Kasaba grave site 07. In your report, you state that in this grave you also found projectiles.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: During your examination-in-chief, you also stated that this grave had the character of a trench, that is to say, like a defence position.

utterances.speaker: JOSE PABLO BARAYBAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.
